newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Setting up new HK government to cost US$14 mln.
newsitem.headline: Setting up new HK government to cost US$14 mln.

text.p: Hong Kong will have to spend just US$14 million to set up its initial post-handover government after China takes the territory back from Britain later this year, its future leader said on Tuesday.

The office of Hong Kong's post-colonial chief executive Tung Chee-hwa said in a statement it was budgeting for set-up costs of HK$107.8 million to prepare government structures over the period from last December 16 to June 30, when British rule ends.

The budget break down was HK$49.4 million for Tung and his office, HK$3 million and HK$42.4 million respectively as honoraria for members of Tung's advisory cabinet and a provisional legislature. There was also HK$13 million put aside for the legislature's staff.
About a third will be paid by the colonial administration as operating expenses for Tung's office and salary for seconded government staff.

The rest, including remuneration for officials not taking office until July 1 and costs related to law drafting and the provisional legislature, will come as an interest-free loan from Beijing, to be repaid after the change in sovereignty.
China set up the provisional legislature to replace the current fully elected council, which Beijing considers illegitimate. It also plans to repeal or amend some human rights laws.
The British colonial administration has denounced both moves and has refused to have anything to do with them.
Hong Kong reverts to Chinese sovereignty at midnight of June 30 after more than 150 years of British rule. ($1 = HK$7.8)
